lacuna.name: gdn-linear-attention-sm75
lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md records this gap twice. Design notes: "GDN linear side recorded as FLA-Triton-served (an sm_75 GDN microbench is its own future item)" and "Out of scope: paged/varlen decode kernel (backlog), Triton/GDN kernel work, d=512 implementation." Execution record: "GDN linear side (75 percent of the 27B's layers): served on sm_75 by FLA Triton kernels (head-shape-generic, CUDA-graph friendly); Triton's tl.dot falls back to FMA below sm_80, so chunked prefill there is FMA-bound - an sm_75 GDN microbench is its own future item, not built here." The 2026-09-06/07 acceptance runs (27B engine gate all-14-green, bridge d=256 landed at 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s) mean the full-attention side now has a measured sm_75 yardstick while the GDN side has none - that asymmetry is the item.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the GDN (Gated DeltaNet) kernel ecosystem is in fast, Qwen-driven motion and every fast path is SM90+; sm_75 rides the FLA Triton reference kernels. (1) flash-linear-attention (fla-org) is the portable substrate: PyPI line 0.4.0 (2025-10-27) -> 0.4.2 (2026-03-12) -> 0.5.0 (2026-04-21) -> 0.5.1 (2026-06-18) -> 0.5.2 (2026-07-27, latest); backend-extras install since v0.5 (bare install no longer pulls torch/triton); benchmarks on GB200; GDN kernels under fla/ops/gated_delta_rule (chunk_gated_delta_rule chunked prefill, fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule decode; chunk size 64 with 16-wide sub-chunk fused kkt+solve_tril kernel). FLA hit a textbook silent-corruption regression: issue #792 (opened 2026-03-26, closed 2026-03-27) '[Bug] Qwen3.5-4B answer "!!!!!!!!!" when using flash-linear-attention 0.5.0' - multimodal generation emitted repeated exclamation marks (text-only looked normal) on git-main installs; root cause per fix PR #794 (branch gdn-fix, merged 2026-03-27, author yzhangcs): the fused chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel (commit baf57d5) produced NaN on partial tail chunks (seq_len % chunk_size != 0) because out-of-bounds positions load g=0 via boundary_check while in-bounds positions carry the cumsum'd gate, exp(0 - g_inbounds) overflows to inf in fp32, and 0 * inf = NaN corrupts the forward substitution; fix adds boundary masks into the tl.where guarding exp/exp2 ('99 NaN without fix -> 0 NaN with fix', 60/60 sweep pass); reporter-confirmed workarounds were pin fla 0.4.2 or disable chunk_gated_delta_rule/fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule; vLLM PR #38315 (2026-03-28) and follow-ups #797/#799/#813 rode the aftermath. (2) FlashQLA (QwenLM, repo created 2026-04-24, 689 stars, pushed 2026-08-26) is the performance frontier: TileLang-built fused warp-specialized GDN chunked-prefill kernels, '2-3x forward speedup and 2x backward speedup over the FLA Triton kernel' on Hopper/Blackwell (benchmarks on H200/GB200 vs FLA 0.5.0 + Triton 3.5.1 + FlashInfer 0.6.9 + TileLang 0.1.8; gains strongest in pretraining and edge-side agentic inference; gate-driven intra-card context parallelism under TP/long-seq/small-head-count). Requirements: 'SM90, SM100, SM103, SM120 or SM121', CUDA 12.8+, PyTorch 2.8+ - a hard sm_75 exclusion. Releases: v0.1.1 (2026-06-30, SM100 + intra-card CP backward, tilelang 0.1.9, aligns with latest FLA interface), v0.1.2 (2026-07-09, SM120 forward; 'now serves as a backend for flash-linear-attention's GDN via the standard FLA API') - i.e. FLA itself can now dispatch into FlashQLA on Hopper+ while Triton kernels remain the sub-8.0 path. (3) FlashInfer shipped its own GDN line: roadmap issue #1690 (opened 2025-09-16 by yzh119, closed Done) -> CuTe-DSL GDN decode kernel PR #2370 -> full CuTe-DSL GDN overhaul (megathread #3491) with v0.6.14 carrying the CuTe-DSL gated-delta-rule rewrite, v0.6.15 adding SM120 context-parallel delta rule; the documented gdn_prefill chunk_gated_delta_rule requires SM90 (Hopper) or SM100 (Blackwell); a newer Blackwell GDN prefill kernel claims up to 5.92x kernel-level / 1.13x end-to-end speedup for Qwen3.5 vs the FLA/Triton path. (4) The sm_75 proof-of-concept exists: weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 (created 2026-05-18, pushed 2026-06-08, 10 stars, 21 commits, MIT) keeps upstream TileLang/SM90 intact and adds a lazy-built hand-written CUDA extension (not TileLang) exposing chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_legacy - forward inference only, scalar-gate GDN, Qwen-style grouped-query head mapping, primary shape D=128, validated on RTX 2080 Ti; SM70 compiles but awaits V100 validation. The same author ships weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (815 stars, base vLLM 0.21.0, fork release v0.1.17, CUDA 12.8 + torch 2.11.0+cu128): Qwen3.6/3.8-27B-FP8 as the primary route on dual modded 2080 Ti 22GB NVLink TP2, 'Qwen3.6 baseline reaching 100+ tok/s single-request decode', MTP3, Marlin FP8/INT4/NVFP4, CUDAGraph - and it integrates both QwenLM/FlashQLA and the SM70/75 legacy kernel ('used by the validated Qwen3.6 prefill profile'; route tables list the fast prefill path as FlashQLA/FlashInfer). (5) TileLang itself became sm_75-capable underneath FlashQLA: v0.1.9 (2026-04-22) fixed T.gemm on SM75 by including SM75 MMA headers (#1956), v0.1.10 (2026-05-25) added native SM75 MMA GEMM (FP16/INT8/INT4), v0.1.12 (2026-07-08) SM75 FP16-accumulate and UINT8 MMA dispatchers (#2392), v0.1.13 (2026-08-03) SM75 GEMM FMA-fallback extension (#2811); latest v0.1.14 (2026-09-02). (6) Triton's posture toward Turing hardened: issue #189 ('Low RTX20 tensor core performance', opened 2021-08-05, STILL OPEN, zero maintainer response) documented ~half-of-cuBLAS matmul throughput on RTX 2080 (M=8192: cuBLAS ~46.5 vs Triton ~24.0 TFLOP/s) with the diagnosis 'Triton is not tuned for Turing. On the RTX2080 it's using the Volta mma.884 instructions which operates at half the throughput of mma.1688'; PR #5066 ('[BACKEND] Deprecate MMAv1; fallback to FMA for computeCapability < 80', merged 2024-11-05, shipped in the 3.3 line, 2025) removed ALL pre-Ampere tensor-core codegen - maintainers stated 'we are not going to break support for older platform but the support will be best effort and won't be tested on our side' and the README floor moved to cc 8.0+; the restore attempt PR #9970 ('[BACKEND] Restore MMA support for Turing GPUs', opened 2026-04-08 by nlzy, closed 2026-04-09 by ThomasRaoux) argued Turing was killed BY ACCIDENT ('Turing uses the MMAv2 layout, so PR #5066 inadvertently killed Turing'), showed sm75 core-test failures dropping 107 -> 54 with the restore, and was declined: 'We don't want to officially support Turing' / 'we don't have any CI machines with sm75'; community forks (Chennesxu/triton-turing, triton-windows) carry Turing MMA out-of-tree. (7) Momentum context: NVIDIA's Gated DeltaNet-2 (2026) continues the layer family [uncertain: details], and vLLM has served Qwen3-Next's hybrid GDN+GQA architecture via FLA since the 2025-09-11 launch blog.
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing today: the entire GDN side of Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8-class hybrids (75 percent of the layers per plan/0007; 48/64 linear in Qwen3-Next-80B) is served by FLA Triton kernels - chunk_gated_delta_rule for prefill/state-init, fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule for decode - under this fork's engine, CUDA-graph friendly and head-shape-generic. GDN-path candidate matrix on sm_75 (dated): (a) FLA Triton chunk kernels - RUNS, the incumbent; codegen fate set by the Triton pin: on Triton >= 3.3 tl.dot emits NO tensor-core math on cc<80 (#5066) - pure FMA fallback, which is the plan's 'FMA-bound chunked prefill' line; on the 3.3.x window there is additionally the f16-conversion LLVM crash on cc<8.0 (#6698, fixed by #7585 merged 2025-07-22, carried from 3.4); on Triton <= 3.2, source-verified at v3.2.0: getMMAVersionSafe maps computeCapability 75-89 to MMAv2, and MMAv2.cpp carries the Turing-native 'mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k8.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32' (fp32-accumulate) and 'm16n8k8.row.col.f16.f16.f16.f16' (fp16-accumulate) PTX - i.e. the house brief's 'Triton never emitted Turing-native mma.1688' is true only for the 2021/1.x era of #189 (mma.884 at half throughput); the correction matters because a Triton pin experiment can recover tensor cores for FLA GDN on sm_75 for free [uncertain: exact first Triton carrying m16n8k8 for sm75, and per-dot admission on 3.2 for every FLA shape]. Caveat inherited from the Marlin-Turing port: fp32-accumulate MMA halves Turing tensor-core throughput, so FLA-style fp32 accumulators ride m16n8k8 at half rate even on 3.2; the full-rate path is the f16-accumulate variant (a numerics decision, not a given). Rough TU102 envelope at the locked 1455 MHz clock: fp16 FMA ceiling ~12.7 TFLOP/s vs ~2x that for f32-acc tensor cores vs ~4x for f16-acc [uncertain: arithmetic estimate] - and the plan/0007 bridge kernel's own measured 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s (m16n8k8, fp32-acc, d=256) is the house yardstick showing what the top of that band looks like in a real kernel; an FMA-only chunk prefill sits an order below it. Turing's 64 KiB smem/SM cap constrains FLA chunk tile configs (num_stages, BM/BN) independently of the codegen question, and Turing has no bf16 tensor cores, so GDN layers ride the fp16 recast contract (overflow-checked >65504 outliers) - FLA's exp/exp2 of cumsum'd (large-negative) gates is exactly where fp16 inf intermediates breed. (b) FlashQLA upstream - NOT viable: SM90/100/103/120/121 + CUDA 12.8 + torch 2.8 hard floor (TileLang warp-specialized/TMA-era kernels); it can, since v0.1.2, serve as FLA's GDN backend on Hopper+ only. (c) FlashInfer GDN (gdn_prefill chunk_gated_delta_rule, CuTe-DSL) - NOT viable: documented SM90/SM100 floor (SM120 CP since 0.6.15); and vLLM's FlashInfer attention backend is itself floored to sm80 on current main (separate drift row). (d) weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 legacy CUDA forward - PROVEN VIABLE on 2080 Ti, the only sm_75-native chunked GDN kernel in existence: kernel timing B=1,T=512,Hq=16,Hv=32,D=128: control recurrent path ~1.126 ms vs legacy ~0.520-0.533 ms = ~2.1x GDN-stage; GGUF-runtime profiling on SM75: fused GDN 406.656 ms -> legacy 195.105 ms (~2.08x) [uncertain: identity of the GGUF runtime, llama.cpp-family inferred]; whole-request: prefill +7.17%, decode +0.61%, wall time -3.49% - the honest calibration that a 2x kernel win moves end-to-end prefill single digits and decode ~nothing (decode already rides the cheap recurrent state update). (e) Engine-level existence proof: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive runs Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 with the legacy GDN prefill on dual 2080 Ti at '100+ tok/s single-request decode' with MTP3 (Reddit r/LocalLLaMA thread: 45 tok/s Qwen3.8-27B MTP3 on a single modded 22GB card [uncertain: date]); on T4-class, vLLM hybrid-GDN serving is reported working but slow (GPTQ INT4 4xT4 guides exist). Measured sm_75 GDN numbers from upstream projects: none - no FLA, FlashInfer, or Qwen benchmark includes Turing; the fork's README numbers above are the only public sm_75 GDN measurements found. Fallback semantics: FLA falls back internally across chunk/fused_recurrent paths and autotunes per shape - substitution changes numerics (different scan order) at fp16-roundoff scale, fine for statistical gates, wrong for bitwise expectations; a silently-wrong path is not hypothetical on this surface (FLA #792 proved the class), so gate-0 discipline applies.

effort_value.effort_estimate: The item as scoped is a microbench, not a kernel campaign: (1) extend the plan/0003/0007 oracle harness to the GDN ops - a float64 torch reference (einsum/recurrent) plus fused_recurrent fp32 as the second agreeing reference for chunk_gated_delta_rule, with tail-chunk cases (T % 64 != 0) and gate-magnitude regressions mandatory per the #792 lesson; (2) a kernel-ladder row: FLA chunk vs fused_recurrent across B/H/D/T at the 27B's shapes, median-of-N, gpu-lease; (3) a Triton-pin A/B (3.2 m16n8k8 vs >=3.4 FMA) in a side venv - the single highest-information cheap experiment; (4) optionally build weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75's legacy forward on the RTX 6000 and put it on the same ladder. Estimate: 1-2 sessions for (1)-(3), +1 for (4). A full sm_75-native GDN kernel (porting FlashQLA-class fusion to CUDA or TileLang) is a plan/0006-scale campaign (weeks) and is NOT this item - it is gated on the microbench showing GDN prefill is a material end-to-end fraction.
effort_value.unlocks: Honest throughput accounting for the operator's actual serving target: the 27B hybrids are 75 percent GDN layers, and every end-to-end number plan/0007 recorded (engine gates, macro gate, PPL) silently bundles unmeasured FMA-bound GDN prefill. The microbench decides three real levers: whether to pin Triton <=3.2 for m16n8k8 GDN prefill (free, if admission holds); whether to adopt the weicj legacy CUDA kernel (proven 2.1x GDN-stage on sibling silicon, forward-only, matches the inference use); and whether a native-kernel campaign is justified at all. It also feeds the tp2 decode bisect campaign (GDN's recurrent decode is part of every step) and any future MTP/spec-decode work, and gives the fork a measured basis to track the fast-moving upstream (FlashQLA/FlashInfer GDN releases) instead of assuming the sm_75 answer.
effort_value.dependency_order: Nothing blocks it: plan/0007 is delivered and explicitly defers this item; the harness (float64 oracle, ladder, gates), the lane venv, and the FLA installation all exist; GPU-lease + median-of-N discipline is standing. External prerequisites are only decisions, already teed up by the drift row: the FLA pin (0.4.2 last-good-pre-regression vs 0.5.2 latest, presumed fixed) and the Triton pin (3.2 vs >=3.4) - both resolvable inside the probe itself. Parallel-safe with everything currently open (the tp2 decode bisect, the FlashInfer floor row); no repo-internal dependencies. If the optional weicj-kernel leg is included, it needs a CUDA build lane for the lazy extension - still self-contained.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness dominates on exactly this surface: FLA #792 is a proven silent-NaN class (0*inf on partial tail chunks in the fused kkt+solve_tril kernel, multimodal prompts only, text-only 'looked normal') - the oracle sweep MUST include T not divisible by chunk_size 64, 16-crossing tail sub-chunks, and extreme gate magnitudes (small gate_logit_normalizer -> very negative cumsums -> exp overflow), and assert finiteness before any timing. Numerics: fp16 recast on Turing (no bf16) sits uneasily next to FLA's exp/exp2-of-cumsum gates (inf intermediates); fp32 accumulation in the chunked scan is the stability anchor; any move to f16-accumulate m16n8k8 for full-rate tensor cores (the Marlin-Turing precedent) trades real precision and needs magnitude-regression gates. Upstream-drift exposure is high and bid-directional: FLA changed API and kernel structure across 0.4->0.5 (regression window, backend extras, FlashQLA-backend dispatch), FlashQLA is three releases hot with an SM90+ floor, Triton has officially exited pre-Ampere (#9970 closed; FMA path 'best effort', untested), and the weicj forks are a 10-star experimental repo (last push 2026-06-08) that may go dark - anything adopted from them is fork-maintained forever. Silent-fallback semantics: FLA's autotuner on sm75 will pick small tile configs under the 64 KiB smem cap (perf risk, not correctness), and chunk vs recurrent substitution changes accumulation order (statistical, not bitwise).
effort_value.determinism_class: Statistical across implementations, bitwise-stable within one: the GDN forward (chunked or recurrent) is an atomic-free, fixed-order scan - no split-K, no atomics - so a pinned kernel config reproduces bitwise across runs and CUDA-graph replays; variance enters through Triton autotune config selection (cache-dependent across warmups/restarts), which must be pinned or logged per transcript, and through backend substitution (chunk vs fused_recurrent vs any CUDA legacy kernel differ at fp16-roundoff scale via different scan/accumulation orders - never compare those bitwise). The float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline maps directly: oracle-check each kernel's math against the fp64 reference (exact comparison in fp64-band, plus explicit finite-asserts for the #792 NaN class), gate throughput on medians across N reps, and record Triton/FLA pins per row so a rebase that re-autotunes or re-lowers (FMA vs m16n8k8) is visible as a step change rather than noise. Restart-to-restart variance on this surface is expected only from autotune-cache persistence and graph-capture sets, not from the kernels themselves.

decision.priority_signal: FOR doing this next: it is the only unmeasured component of the operator's primary serving target (75 percent of the 27B's layers ride it in every recorded number); the ecosystem window is actively closing - Triton officially exited pre-Ampere (#9970 closed 2026-04-09, FMA-only 'best effort'), FlashQLA/FlashInfer GDN kernels are all-in on SM90+, and the weicj sm_75 adaptation (2.1x GDN-stage, 100+ tok/s 27B engine on sibling Turing silicon) exists NOW while being small enough (10 stars, forward-only, last push 2026-06-08) to disappear; and the cheapest lever (Triton 3.2 pin recovering m16n8k8 for FLA dots) is pure information the fork currently lacks. AGAINST: the one whole-request measurement that exists (weicj's own) says the ceiling is modest - wall time -3.49%, decode +0.61% - suggesting GDN prefill is not the binding constraint at typical service lengths on 2080 Ti-class parts; the tp2 decode bisect is a hotter open front with a live RED verdict; and FLA-Triton demonstrably works on sm_75 today, so this is an optimization/accounting item, not an availability item. Net: do the probe-and-pin experiment soon (1-2 sessions, oracle-first), defer any native-kernel campaign until the microbench shows a material end-to-end fraction.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe, oracle-first, no timing until numerics are green, under a day on the existing TU102 host: (1) reference pair - torch fp64 gated-deltanet (sequential reference implementation, chunk-math-free) AND FLA fused_recurrent fp32 as the second agreeing reference; (2) differential sweep of chunk_gated_delta_rule on sm_75 over B in {1,8}, T in {511, 512, 513, 75, 4096, 32768} (T % 64 != 0 cases mandatory), Hv/Hq at the 27B shape (GVA 32/16-class), D=128, with gate_logit_normalizer swept small/large; assert max rel-err in fp64 band AND all-finite - any NaN/garbage disqualifies that FLA pin outright (this is the #792 tripwire); repeat on fla 0.4.2 and 0.5.2 to settle the pin. (3) Only then time, median-of-5, exclusive lease: chunk vs recurrent across T=512..32768, ms/token, plus the Triton-pin A/B (3.2 vs >=3.4 in side venvs) inspecting emitted PTX/SASS for mma vs ffma; (4) optional leg: build weicj FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 legacy forward on the same card and put it on the ladder under the same oracle. Deliverable: a dated ledger row (GDN-stage ms/token, GDN share of a 27B engine step from the plan/0007 transcripts, pin verdicts) that either closes the item ('FLA-Triton is within X of the bridge-kernel envelope, no campaign warranted') or scopes the native-kernel campaign with a number.
